title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 8 (manuscript p.24) gives a canonical way to realize a 'regular n-gon' P_n inside a complex projective line Σ. Here P_n is a combinatorial polygon, a triple P = (S, A, R ⊂ S×A) of vertices, edges and incidence relation. The construction has four steps.

1. Take a regular 2n-gon P̃_{2n} embedded in a real Euclidean plane V = V_{P̃_{2n}}, centred at the origin.
2. The map -1 on V induces the antipodal involution of the combinatorial 2n-gon. The quotient P̃_{2n}/{±1} is an n-gon P_n, with S = S̃/±1, A = Ã/±1 and R = R̃/±1.
3. Put Σ = P(V)(ℂ), the complexified projective line. A vertex s̃ ↦ ℝ·s̃ ↦ ℂ·s̃ ∈ P(V_ℂ) = P(V)(ℂ) gives a map S̃ → Σ that is constant on antipodal pairs. It therefore descends to an embedding S ↪ Σ.
4. This map factors through the real points Σ_ℝ = P(V)(ℝ), a circle. Since a line in V is determined by an angle mod π, and θ ↦ 2θ identifies P(V)(ℝ) with the unit circle, the n lines through opposite vertex pairs become n equally spaced points on the equator of the Riemann sphere. After choosing a coordinate these are the n-th roots of unity.

Grothendieck remarks that Σ_{P̃_{2n}} = P(V_{P̃_{2n}}) really depends only on P_n, so it can be written Σ_{P_n}.

The next page continues the thread. D_{2n} = Aut_comb(P̃_{2n}) acts linearly on V and hence on Σ. The centre ±1 acts trivially, so the action factors through D_{P_n} = D_{2n}/±1 ≅ D_n, which is the natural action by transport of structure. For n odd the extension 1 → ±1 → D_{2n} → D_n → 1 splits; a splitting corresponds to choosing one of the two inscribed n-gons.

Purpose in the manuscript: a canonical, symmetric model of the regular n-gon (equivalently the 'dihedral' map with two n-gonal faces, the two hemispheres) on CP^1. It feeds the Teichmüller-style analysis of n-gonal and P-weighted maps and their automorphism groups, which the previous page relates to the corresponding fundamental groups.
errors: No mathematical errors. Minor implicit point: 'regular' needs a Euclidean (or at least conformal plus D_{2n}-invariant) structure on V. The n points on P(V)(ℝ) are pinned down up to projective equivalence by the D_n-symmetry rather than by the combinatorics alone. Grothendieck's claim that Σ depends only on P_n is consistent with this, but on this page it is asserted, not proved.

ideas.what: Regular n-gon on CP^1 obtained as the projectivization of a centred regular 2n-gon: vertices = real lines through antipodal vertex pairs, lying on the real circle P(V)(ℝ)
ideas.modern_name: n-th roots of unity on the equator of the Riemann sphere; dihedral map / dihedral dessin (Belyi map z^n)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses regular maps and dessins in general; this specific construction is not known to be published

ideas.what: Combinatorial polygon as a triple (S, A, R ⊂ S×A), with the quotient of a 2n-gon by the antipodal involution
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial map / flag description of polygons; quotient by the central involution

ideas.what: Action of D_{2n} on P(V) factoring through D_{2n}/±1 ≅ D_n, with the extension splitting for n odd (next page)
ideas.modern_name: dihedral subgroups of PGL_2; the isomorphism D_{2n} ≅ D_n × C_2 for n odd

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary, classical construction (the regular n-gon on the real circle of CP^1 via the doubling map from a centred 2n-gon). The value is only expository, showing Grothendieck's intrinsic, 'transport of structure' style of setting up the groundwork. Nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Over 'à n côtés' the superscript 'P_n' labels the polygon. Over 'complexe' the superscript 'Σ' names the sphere.
'(centré aux pour polygônes réguliers)' is probably '(centré, comme pour polygones réguliers)' or similar; the reading is uncertain.
In the map S̃ → Σ, R_{s̃} most likely denotes the real line ℝ·s̃ through the vertex s̃, sent to its complexification ℂ·R_{s̃} ∈ P(V_ℂ) = P(V)(ℂ).
The heading line for (4) reads 'l'application (3) se factorise par' followed by a crossed-out symbol, then (4) Σ_ℝ = Σ_{P̃_{2n}}(ℝ).
